content_of_post_to_comment: Tell someone two things can be true at once and watch them accidentally reveal whether they think in binaries or relationships. Binary thinking asks: Which one is true? Who is right? What must be rejected so the other thing can stand? Relational thinking asks: How do these truths interact? What changes when they are held together? What becomes visible in the tension between them? A person can love you and still harm you. A boundary can be compassionate and disappointing. Grief and gratitude can enter the same room. Someone can be responsible for their behaviour and still shaped by what happened to them. Holding two truths is not confusion. It is often the point where our understanding of reality becomes more complete. The question is not always which truth wins. Sometimes the question is what kind of understanding becomes possible when neither one has to disappear.
comment: A further tension is that holding two truths requires knowing where integration ends and tolerance begins. Complexity can deepen compassion, but it can also become a way to avoid naming harm clearly.
